title: Understanding Wave-Particle Duality
text:
Quantum particles, such as photons and electrons, exhibit a characteristic known as wave-particle duality. This means that these entities do not behave purely as classical particles (localized points) nor purely as waves (distributed fluctuations), but rather possess properties of both depending on the experimental context.

Measurement plays a crucial role in this phenomenon; when observed, particles often appear to behave as discrete particles. Conversely, through techniques like interferometry, they demonstrate wave-like patterns. The uncertainty principle, introduced by Heisenberg, further solidifies this concept, stating that pairs of properties (like position and momentum) cannot be simultaneously known with perfect accuracy.
